reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) does not address CoCrFeNiTi, its deformation mechanisms, or the effect of annealing on nanoscale ordering/precipitates in this system. E1 discusses deformation twins in CrCoNi and CrMnFeCoNi, E2 concerns a refractory BCC HEA, and E3 describes magnetic/electrical properties of FeCoNi(AlSi)x. None supports the specific premises about dislocation motion, lattice distortion, or heat-treatment response in CoCrFeNiTi.
premises: Low hardness/strength in as-cast CoCrFeNiTi solid solution is due to unhindered dislocation motion
Unhindered motion arises from low intrinsic lattice distortion and lack of nanoscale obstacles
Annealing at ~600 °C can induce nanoscale ordering or fine precipitates in this alloy
Such nanoscale features act as obstacles that pin dislocations and increase strength
The strengthening can be achieved without completely sacrificing ductility
